items.title: Tesla's Model 3 and Model Y can be a backup battery for your house
items.snippet: Some Tesla Model 3 and Model Y owners can use their EV battery to keep the lights on longer during a power outage, now that Tesla's expanding the Powershare Home Backup feature. items.snippet: Since 2023, Apple's newer iPhones have had an 80 percent charge limit for those who want to extend battery lifespan. Charging to 80 percent instead of 100 percent is supposed to put less stress on the battery, improving longevity. For the last three years, I've used that setting on my iPhone. I started with the iPhone 15 Pro Max , then did the iPhone 16 Pro Max , and most recently, the iPhone 17 Pro Max. After 12 months at an 80 percent maximum charge, my iPhone 17 Pro Max is at 97 percent maximum capacity with a cycle count of 277. items.snippet: Yesterday we reported that Apple tripled the number of iCloud Mail aliases users can create, from three to nine . items.title: Today in Apple history: Michael Dell says he'd shut down Apple
items.snippet: October 6, 1997: Michael Dell makes an incredibly bleak appraisal of Apple’s fortunes, uttering a quote that will become notorious. Asked what he would do with the struggling company, the founder of Dell Inc. says he would “shut it down and give the money back to the shareholders.” As incorrect forecasts go, this ultimately will go down as one of the more notable in tech history. But it doesn’t seem that way at the time. Sometimes even the tech industry’s smartest people prove spectacularly bad at seeing what comes next. In 1997, Michael Dell had plenty of reason to think Apple was finished. The company was hemorrhaging money, its product strategy was an utter mess, and Apple co-founder Steve Jobs had just returned to the company he’d been forced out of a decade and a half before. What Dell didn’t know was that Apple was standing at the edge of one of the greatest turnarounds in business history — and his throwaway remark would become a perfect reminder that even industry giants can mistake a company’s darkest moment for its final chapter. USB-C is no one-trick pony—handling data transfer, video output and power input. You’ll find faster variants of USB-C (called Thunderbolt 3, 4 or 5) on Macs. items.title: The upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro may be Air-light
items.snippet: Macworld After years of rumors and speculation, it looks like the first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen is finally almost here. If the latest leaks are to be believed, the device is currently in testing within Apple on macOS 27.2, and should arrive within the next month or so. This new MacBook Pro won’t just be a current model with a touchscreen. items.title: Windows 11 gains ground as price hike looms for Windows 10 security updates
items.snippet: According to new figures from Statcounter , Windows 11 continues to gain users at the expense of Windows 10. The newer operating system is now estimated to account for 71.5% of all Windows computers globally, while Windows 10 has dropped to 27.8%, reports The Register . Microsoft itself does not publish any user figures. Statcounter’s estimates are based on tracking code installed on websites globally. These figures are not broken out by consumer and business use. A major shift to Windows 11 occurred when mainstream support for Windows 10 ended on October 14, 2025. Just a month before that transition, about half of PCs still ran Windows 10 , according to executives from Dell and HP. Since th

items.title: OpenAI to begin watermarking AI-generated text
items.snippet: OpenAI has announced that within a few weeks it will introduce a digital watermark for text generated using the company’s AI tools, ChatGPT and Codex. This move comes in response to the EU’s new AI regulations, introduced two months ago, which stipulate that AI-generated content must be identifiable . Competitor Anthropic introduced a similar feature for its AI tools in August. OpenAI’s new watermark will be available worldwide, but it is enabled by default only within the EU. In other words, users in other parts of the world can ignore it. According to TechCrunch , it appears possible to edit out the watermark, so it remains to be seen whether it serves any significant purpose. This article

They may also be unsure which tools and data they can use or how to test new technology without creating security problems or disrupting the business. items.title: Windows 365 new features: Reserve, disaster recovery, display protection, and AVD Hybrid
items.snippet: Microsoft's September 2026 recap for Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) lists about two dozen changes. Several of them matter for daily administration: user-initiated provisioning for Windows 365 Reserve, business continuity and disaster recovery settings in Cloud PC configurations, local admin rights in Cloud PC configurations, display protection, TWAIN scanner redirection, and AVD Hybrid. Microsoft's recap is written like a marketing summary, so this article looks at the Microsoft Learn documentation to find out what you must configure and where the limits are. Some features are still in preview. Source

items.title: Enable built-in Sysmon in Windows 11 with PowerShell
items.snippet: Windows 11 now includes System Monitor (Sysmon), a tool that logs process creation, network connections, and file creation time changes to the Windows event log. Previously, it was a separate download from Sysinternals. The built-in version is an optional feature that is disabled by default, so you must enable it with PowerShell and install it with the sysmon command. This article explains the prerequisites, the commands, how to apply your own XML configuration, and how to verify that Sysmon writes events. Source

It is not a full Microsoft exit: Outlook and other Microsoft services will remain in use. Source

items.title: Atlassian brings GPT-6 models to Rovo as Jira agents remain in development
items.snippet: Atlassian is a software company that makes tools for managing projects, collaborating, and sharing knowledge at work. It is best known for Jira and Confluence, which help teams track what needs doing and document what they know. Atlassian and OpenAI are expanding their partnership to bring GPT-6 models, including GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6, to AI agents across Atlassian’s platform and Rovo. Rovo is Atlassian’s AI assistant, combining OpenAI models with the Teamwork Graph to draw on company context. Deeper Jira integrations that let teams assign work to agents are still being explored. Source

items.title: LibreOffice makes “no AI” a feature—and sets a high bar for adding it

The suite works without an internet connection, and users can opt in to AI through extensions that connect to local models. Source

items.title: Vercel confirms KVM zero-day that may let guests seize host root
items.snippet: Vercel has confirmed a KVM zero-day reported through its Sandbox bug bounty program, with researcher Paulos Yibelo claiming it enables a virtual machine to escape and gain root access on its host. Vercel Sandbox runs Firecracker microVMs on KVM, but the vulnerability’s technical details and affected versions have not been made public. There is not yet enough information to determine which KVM deployments are affected or what fix administrators should apply. Source

items.title: ClickFix cache smuggling bypasses Windows Run’s 260-character limit
items.snippet: ClickFix attackers are using compromised websites to stash malicious scripts in browser caches, bypassing the Windows Run dialog’s roughly 260-character limit. A short command pasted by the victim retrieves the cached payload instead of downloading it at execution time. Microsoft says the chain proceeds through PowerShell and in-memory.NET code to target browser and device credentials. Source

items.title: Public MCP servers expose data to risky jurisdictions and expired domains
items.snippet: A scan of 15,465 public MCP servers found an overlooked risk for organizations adopting AI agents: some may send data to unapproved jurisdictions, while others could be hijacked through expired domains. The servers use the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which connects AI models and agents to tools and data. The findings point to weak marketplace safeguards and a need for organizations to verify the servers their agents use. Source

items.title: Microsoft's Xbox Elite Series 3 Controller Leaks Again
items.snippet: Microsoft’s upcoming Xbox Elite Series 3 Controller has appeared in a new datamined leak coming from Microsoft’s Xbox Design Lab website. The new controller first appeared in leaked pictures from Brazil’s National Telecommunications Agency, then a Redditor posted pictures of a prototype unit that showed a tiny built-in screen on top of the controller, as well as two new scroll wheels at the bottom. Well, according to these latest details shared on Reddit, Microsoft’s new Xbox Elite Controller will offer Hall Effect and TMR sticks. These two technologies reduce the risk of wear and stick drift by relying on magnets. The new leak also mentions the inclusion of “Impulse Triggers (ERMs) & Advanced Haptics (VCAs) Motors,” which suggest that Microsoft may try to replicate the haptic feedback technology on Sony’s DualSense controllers for the PS5. There’s also the mention of an audio scroll wheel, which may correspond to the new wheels near the headphone jack we saw in previous leaked pictures. items.title: GTT bets that the network, not the log file, is where AI-era security gets won
items.snippet: Security teams face a time problem, and AI is making it worse. Attackers use AI to find flaws and write exploits faster than any human-staffed security operations center can respond, while most defensive tools still collect telemetry, ship it somewhere, normalize it, and only then analyze it. Each step adds delay, and in security, delay is exposure. GTT Communications believes the answer is to stop moving data and place intelligence where network traffic already is. items.title: Micro data center company launches stackable data center for edge and AI
items.snippet: Australian micro data center specialist Zella DC has introduced a modular data center platform designed to bring more computing capacity into locations where conventional racks and purpose-built facilities are difficult to deploy. Called Zella Stack, the new system uses a stackable architecture that lets customers begin with a relatively small amount of infrastructure and add capacity as computing requirements grow. The company unveiled the platform at Yotta 2026 in Las Vegas. The approach is aimed at edge computing deployments , where space, installation time, and physical access can be significant challenges. The Zella Stack modules are 12RU containers that measure approximately 51.2 × 27.

items.title: From automated response to reasoning: Building confidence in AI-driven NetOps
items.snippet: The concept of probabilistic automation can be off-putting, even divisive. Consider self-driving cars. They’re part of the progression of vehicle automation that includes parallel parking assist, driver assistance and hands-free driving. However, when it comes to self-driving cars, getting on board requires a huge leap of faith that many people aren’t willing to take.
